skill.name: bioservices
skill.description: Use BioServices to query UniProt, KEGG, ChEMBL, PubChem, Reactome, QuickGO, and related bioinformatics services from Python workflows.
skill.summary: Query and combine major bioinformatics databases through BioServices Python workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static findings are almost entirely false positives caused by biological identifier names, Markdown backticks, documentation examples, and expected result exports. No prompt-injection text or malicious command execution was found. One medium privacy risk remains because BLAST workflows submit sequence data and an email address to an external service.

remediation.suggestion: Add a clear consent note before BLAST and other third-party API calls. Recommend --skip-blast for proprietary or sensitive sequences.
Document which services receive identifiers or compound names, including UniProt, KEGG, ChEMBL, QuickGO, PSICQUIC, and NCBI.
Recommend dedicated output directories and warn users before writing over existing result files.

semantic_findings.title: External Bioinformatics Data Submission
semantic_findings.description: The protein workflow submits a protein sequence and user email address to the NCBI BLAST service. This is expected functionality, but it can disclose sensitive research data to a third-party service.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly passes sequence and email values into NCBIblast.run, and the skill documentation shows the same workflow. The risk is privacy exposure, not malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Bioinformatics work often requires repeated queries across disconnected public databases. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through BioServices workflows for proteins, pathways, compounds, and identifiers.
actual_capabilities: Query UniProt for protein entries, sequences, annotations, and identifier mappings.
Use KEGG workflows for pathway discovery, pathway parsing, and interaction export.
Search compounds in KEGG and cross-reference ChEBI and ChEMBL identifiers.
Run batch identifier conversion with chunking, retry logic, and CSV output.
Retrieve Gene Ontology annotations through QuickGO examples and scripts.
Combine multiple BioServices APIs into documented research workflows.
limitations: Requires the external bioservices Python package and network access to public databases.
Database availability, rate limits, and response formats can change outside the skill.
BLAST workflows can take several minutes and require a user email address.
The included scripts are examples and may need validation for production pipelines.

use_cases.title: Characterize a Protein
use_cases.description: Find a UniProt entry, retrieve sequence data, map pathways, and collect GO annotations for one protein.

use_cases.title: Map Research Identifiers
use_cases.description: Convert batches of UniProt, KEGG, Ensembl, RefSeq, PDB, and GO identifiers into target database IDs.

use_cases.title: Cross-Reference Compounds
use_cases.description: Search a compound by name and collect KEGG, ChEBI, ChEMBL, formula, mass, and pathway information.

prompt_templates.title: Find Protein Information
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the BioServices skill to look up [protein name or UniProt ID]. Return the UniProt ID, gene name, organism, sequence availability, and key annotations.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Identifier List
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the batch identifier workflow to convert my [source database] IDs to [target database]. Explain input format, chunk size, output columns, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Pathways
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the KEGG pathway workflow for organism code [organism code]. Summarize pathway counts, interaction types, export files, and rate-limit precautions.

prompt_templates.title: Build Multi-Service Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a BioServices workflow that starts with [protein, gene, or compound], maps related database IDs, retrieves annotations, and lists validation checks before saving results.

output_examples.input: Analyze ZAP70_HUMAN with protein, pathway, and GO workflows.
output_examples.output: The result identifies the UniProt entry, reports sequence availability, lists matching KEGG pathways, and groups GO terms by biological process, molecular function, and cellular component.

output_examples.input: Convert a text file of UniProt accessions to KEGG identifiers.
output_examples.output: The result describes the source and target databases, total identifiers processed, successful mappings, failed mappings, and the CSV columns saved for review.
The result summarizes the selected KEGG compound, ChEBI identifier, ChEMBL identifier, molecular properties, and any related pathway references.

best_practices: Use organism filters when searching gene symbols to reduce ambiguous matches.
Add delays and chunk large batches to respect public database limits.
Review external data-sharing requirements before submitting sequences or emails.
anti_patterns: Do not send proprietary sequences to BLAST without explicit approval.
Do not assume the first database match is correct for ambiguous names.
Do not overwrite important files with default output names.

faq.question: What is BioServices?
faq.answer: BioServices is a Python package for accessing many bioinformatics web services through a unified API.

faq.question: Which databases does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers workflows for UniProt, KEGG, ChEMBL, ChEBI, PubChem, Reactome, QuickGO, PSICQUIC, and related services.

faq.question: Does it run analysis locally only?
faq.answer: No. Most workflows query public web services, so identifiers, sequences, or compound names may leave the local machine.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Can it convert many identifiers at once?
faq.answer: Yes. The batch converter reads one identifier per line, processes chunks, retries failures, and exports mapping results.

faq.question: Is BLAST optional?
faq.answer: Yes. The protein workflow supports skipping BLAST, which is useful for sensitive sequences or faster runs.
